title: Recovery of low derivatives by degree-block induction
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field, $A=L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in A$ have positive orders $d_i$. Fix pairwise incomparable vertices $a_i\in\mathbf N^n$ with $|a_i|=d_i$, ordered by nondecreasing degree. Let $D= igcup_i((0,a_i)+\mathbf N^{m+n})$, and let $k_1<\cdots<k_p$ be the distinct $d_i$. For each $\ell$, let $Z^\ell$ be the transverse variables occurring in some $a_i$ with $d_i\le k_\ell$, and write $V_\ell=(Z_j:Z_j\in Z^\ell)$. Suppose for every $j\in Z^\ell$ one can choose $i(\ell,j)$ and $ eta_{\ell,j}\in\mathbf N^n$ with $d_{i(\ell,j)}\le k_\ell$, $a_{i(\ell,j)}= eta_{\ell,j}+e_j$, and $g_{\ell,j}=\partial_Z^{ eta_{\ell,j}}f_{i(\ell,j)}\in V_\ell$. Suppose the constant $Z^\ell$-Jacobian of $(g_{\ell,j})_{j\in Z^\ell}$ has nonzero determinant in $L$. Fix $Q\ge\max_i(d_i-1)$. For each $\ell$ and $d_i>k_\ell$, assume $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\delta}f_i\in V_\ell$ whenever $|\delta|\le Q$ and $\delta$ belongs to the diagram generated by the projections to $Z^\ell$ of the vertices with $d_j\le k_\ell$. All derivatives use [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Let $I_t\subset A$, $t\ge0$, be an increasing family of ideals such that for every $i$, $t<d_i$, and $\gamma
otin D$ with $|\gamma|\le t$,
$$\partial^\gamma f_i\in I_t+(\partial^\alpha f_i:\alpha\in D,\ |\alpha|\le t).$$
Then for every block $\ell$,
$$(g_{\ell,j}:j\in Z^\ell)=V_\ell\subseteq I_{k_\ell-1},\qquad (\partial^
u f_i:d_i\le k_\ell,\ |
u|<d_i)\subseteq I_{k_\ell-1}.$$
In particular $(\partial^
u f_i:|
u|<d_i)\subseteq I_{\max_i d_i-1}$ when $s>0$. The assertion permits empty essential-variable sets, and is vacuous for $s=0$; no supported generation or Taylor-matrix presentation is assumed.

proof.text: Use strong induction on the numerical degree b, only asserting conclusions when b occurs among the vertices. For a generator of degree b, a diagram exponent gamma of degree at most b-1 dominates some vertex a_j of smaller degree c. Apply the induction assertion at this occurring c, rather than choosing the immediately preceding block.

proof.text: Restrict gamma to transverse coordinates essential at degree c, obtaining delta, and put rho=gamma-fullVertex(delta). The vertex a_j is supported on these essential coordinates, so delta belongs to inDiagram a c and has degree at most Q. The later-generator hypothesis gives partial^delta f_i in transverseIdeal a c. Each complementary coordinate derivative preserves this ideal by ideal-span induction and the Leibniz rule. Coordinate derivatives commute by their coefficient formulas; list permutation of the defining iterated derivatives proves partial^(delta+rho)=partial^rho partial^delta. Hence partial^gamma f_i lies in the earlier transverse ideal and thus in I_(b-1).

proof.text: For every lower derivative outside the diagram apply the reduction hypothesis at t=b-1. Every diagram derivative generating its right-hand ideal lies in I_(b-1) by the preceding step, so the whole right side is contained in I_(b-1). Earlier generators use the strong induction assertion and monotonicity. This proves containment of the span of all lower derivatives of generators with degree at most b.

proof.text: Prove the needed zero-graph ideal equality directly, without formal substitution or reindexing: membership of each selected g_j in the coordinate ideal gives g_j=sum_l C_jl X_l by the finite ideal-span formula. Applying a coordinate derivative and constant coefficient shows constantCoeff C_jl=constantCoeff(partial_l g_j), since all X_l have zero constant term. The assumed nonzero Jacobian determinant implies constantCoeff(det C) is a unit, hence det C is a unit in the power-series ring. Its nonsingular inverse expresses every coordinate X_l as a linear combination of the g_j; therefore their ideals agree. Each selected derivative has degree d_pick-1 by the vertex equation and the degree-mapDomain formula, so the previous lower-derivative containment puts this equal coordinate ideal in I_(b-1). This also treats an empty coordinate tuple.

proof.text: When s>0 the finite family of degrees has a maximum attained at some vertex. Apply the lower-derivative assertion at this degree and include every generator using Finset.le_sup. When s=0 there are no occurring blocks and the final assertion has false premise. Positive degrees justify b-1<b for each occurring block. The original hypotheses, including order, incomparability and the ordering of the vertex family, are unchanged.
